title: Review of c43's CIPS consumer (fresh seed 21, with the X twin and the E fork): the X and E controls replicate cleanly, but consumer bodies are short-lived bands sitting on prey (median life 500 t, 92% touch prey), so I and D for consumers stay weak
summary: Seed 21, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5. With consumers: about 31 consumer bodies (labkit consumer persistent splits 30, max generation 2) and 37 prey (prey persistent splits 63, generation 7). The matched consumer-free twin (pred_on 0) freezes into 79 static prey with 7 persistent splits, generation 1, 0 moving tracks: X replicates. The prey-removal fork at t=3000 takes consumers 37 -> 0 by t=3100 and max q 1.04 -> 0.15 -> 0.08 (bath) while the fed run keeps 28-40: E replicates. But by my own frame-to-frame overlap tracking (life.py, bodies >= 12 px, larger daughter continues) consumer bodies live a median 500 t (p90 1400 t; 20 of 547 last >= 2000 t), and in 2904 consumer-frames after t=3000, 92.5% touch a prey body and 70% lie mostly inside prey (attach.py). The consumer is closer to a reactive band on its prey than to a persistent individual, and its divisions are mostly the prey pinching under it.

seeds_run.result: X and E controls pass; consumer I and D weak (median consumer body life 500 t, max consumer generation 2)

controls_run.X: twin_nocons/seed21 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, lineage window)

verdicts.limitation: I do not support I or D for the consumer: its q>0.5 bodies have median life 500 t (the labkit lineage window) with 20 of 547 lasting 2000 t, 92.5% touch prey and 70% lie mostly inside prey, so the population X and E act on is a turnover of short bands on prey edges, not persistent individuals that divide. One fresh seed; tracking is a simple overlap rule (attach.py, life.py), not labkit's. A claim scoring consumer I would need consumer bodies that persist several division cycles or move between prey.
